holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.note: Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Human Rights Day
holidays.note: Marks the Sharpeville massacre of 1960, when police killed 69 people protesting against the pass laws. The constitution was signed at Sharpeville in 1996.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.note: A Christian holy day. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Family Day
holidays.note: Easter Monday, renamed Family Day in the 1994 holidays law.

holidays.name: Freedom Day
holidays.note: Marks the first election in which all South Africans could vote, on 27 April 1994.

holidays.name: Workers' Day
holidays.note: International May Day, recognised as a public holiday in South Africa from 1995.

holidays.name: Youth Day
holidays.note: Marks the Soweto uprising of 1976, when police fired on schoolchildren protesting against being taught in Afrikaans.

holidays.name: National Women's Day
holidays.note: Marks the march of about 20,000 women to the Union Buildings in 1956 against pass laws for women.

holidays.name: Heritage Day
holidays.note: Kept in KwaZulu-Natal as Shaka Day, the date traditionally given for King Shaka's death. It became Heritage Day, for all South Africans' cultures, in 1995. Many people now mark it with a braai.

holidays.name: Day of Reconciliation
holidays.note: 16 December carries two histories. Afrikaner nationalists kept it as Dingane's Day and later the Day of the Covenant (or Vow), remembering Blood River in 1838. In 1961 the ANC's armed wing chose the same date to launch its struggle. Since 1995 it has been a day to hold both, and to work towards reconciliation.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.note: A Christian holy day. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Day of Goodwill
holidays.note: Boxing Day, renamed the Day of Goodwill in the 1994 holidays law.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.note: A bank holiday in Scotland since 1871, and in England, Wales and Northern Ireland since 1974. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.note: A traditional holiday in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and a bank holiday in Scotland since 1871. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Easter Monday
holidays.note: One of the first bank holidays, in 1871 (not in Scotland).

holidays.name: Early May Bank Holiday
holidays.note: Scotland has had a holiday on the first Monday in May since 1871. England, Wales and Northern Ireland followed in 1978, linked to international May Day.

holidays.name: Spring Bank Holiday
holidays.note: Replaced Whit Monday, one of the original 1871 bank holidays, from 1971.

holidays.name: Summer Bank Holiday
holidays.date: The last Monday in August (first Monday in Scotland)
holidays.note: The 1871 act set it on the first Monday in August. England, Wales and Northern Ireland moved it to the last Monday from 1971.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.note: A Christian holy day and traditional holiday. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Boxing Day
holidays.note: A bank holiday in England, Wales and Ireland since 1871.

holidays.name: St Andrew's Day (Scotland)
holidays.note: Scotland's patron saint's day, made a bank holiday by the Scottish Parliament in 2007. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: St Patrick's Day (Northern Ireland)
holidays.note: Ireland's patron saint's day, a bank holiday since 1903. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Battle of the Boyne (Northern Ireland)
holidays.note: Also called Orangemen's Day. Marks William III's victory over James II in 1690 — a date that still divides communities in Northern Ireland. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Remembrance Sunday
holidays.note: Not a bank holiday. Remembers the dead of the world wars and later conflicts, with two minutes of silence — also kept at 11 a.m. on 11 November, the hour the First World War ended.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.note: One of the four original federal holidays of 1870. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.

holidays.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
holidays.note: Honours Martin Luther King Jr., born on 15 January 1929. Signed into law in 1983 and first observed in 1986.

holidays.name: Washington's Birthday (Presidents' Day)
holidays.note: Officially Washington's Birthday — he was born on 22 February 1732 — and a federal holiday since 1879. Moved to a Monday in 1971, it is widely called Presidents' Day.

holidays.name: Memorial Day
holidays.note: Began after the Civil War as Decoration Day, when people decorated soldiers' graves. A federal holiday since 1888; it now honours all Americans who died in military service.

holidays.name: Juneteenth
holidays.note: Marks 19 June 1865, when news of freedom reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas. Celebrated by Black communities for over 150 years before it became a federal holiday in 2021.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.note: Marks the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on 4 July 1776.

holidays.name: Labor Day
holidays.note: Honours working people. Unlike most countries, the US marks it in September rather than on 1 May — even though May Day grew from the Haymarket affair in Chicago.

holidays.name: Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day
holidays.note: Marks Columbus's landing in the Americas in 1492, which is older than Weft's timeline. Observed nationally since the 1930s and a federal holiday since 1968; many states and cities now keep it as Indigenous Peoples' Day instead, and in 2021 the president issued the first proclamation recognising that day.

holidays.name: Veterans Day
holidays.note: Began as Armistice Day, marking the end of the First World War, and was renamed Veterans Day in 1954 to honour all who served.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving
holidays.note: Traced to a harvest feast shared by English settlers and Wampanoag people at Plymouth in 1621, which is older than Weft's timeline. Presidents proclaimed days of thanksgiving from 1789; Lincoln made it a yearly national holiday in 1863, and a 1941 law fixed it on the fourth Thursday. Since 1970, many Native Americans have kept the same day as a National Day of Mourning.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.note: One of the four original federal holidays of 1870. Its origins are older than 1700, where Weft's timeline begins.
